_meta: DRAFT — NOT YET IMPORTED (wired automatically by the gen-slices auto-loader). Africa-branch municipal-fiscal-tier push, round AF/G.23, 2026-08-13. Eswatini's dual Tinkhundla (rural/regional, via 4 Regions -> Tinkhundla -> Chiefdoms) / urban-council (15 gazetted Urban Local Governments under the Urban Government Act No. 8 of 1969) local-government system, both substantiated this round with real named-unit fiscal documents: a Ministry of Housing and Urban Development report itemizing individual town boards/councils/municipalities with real grant figures, Mbabane Municipal Council's own audited financial statements, the Auditor-General naming Manzini Municipal Council's loan balances, and the Ministry of Tinkhundla Administration and Development's own per-region Regional Development Fund table. Two of the richest sources (both parliament.gov.sz) required a `curl --insecure` workaround this round due to a broken TLS certificate chain on that domain — flagged in each affected node's description as a hosting/technical-access caveat only, not a content problem. All findings below were downloaded and full-text-extracted for verification by the research pass that preceded this synthesis (not tool-summarized only), per that pass's own methodology note.

reports.title: Annual Performance Report, Financial Year 2024/25
reports.publisher: Ministry of Housing and Urban Development, Kingdom of Eswatini
reports.description: Ministry of Housing and Urban Development's own FY2024/25 performance report to Parliament, naming individual urban local governments with real budget/grant figures -- the 'higher tier reporting on named lower-tier units' pattern. On the Capital Improvement Programme grant (Project X480/99): 'Government has allocated E20 million emalangeni for capital improvement expenditure for the under listed towns this current financial year... The allocation of the government CIP grant to the above listed local authorities is subject to their obtaining a positive grading in their annual organizational performance assessment' -- naming Lavumisa Town Board, Mankayane Town Board, Ngwenya Town Board, Vuvulane Town Board and Malkerns Town Council as recipients of E4,000,000.00 each (E20,000,000.00 total). On the two City/Municipal Councils: 'The immediate cut off of subventions grant allocation to Mbabane and Manzini municipalities this reporting year, disrupting their annual budget plans,' and separately, of Mbabane: 'Council is being owed in excess of E90 million in rates by Government, including rates from the previous years.' On Nhlangano Town Council: 'Nhlangano Town Council operates on projected budget of E27.03 million. The budget is realized from property taxation (both government and private property), own source of revenue and government subvention' (General Grant line = E711,000.00 against total budgeted income of E27,039,423). On Siteki Town Council: 'The activities that are meant to assist the town council to attain the vision are financed by property rates contributing 77%, government subvention 4%, user fees and charges 18.8%. The total annual budget for Local Authority is E17,175,616, including capital grant of E2,000,000.' On Manzini Municipal Council: a budgeted 'Recurrent Grant' line of E3,677,400 against total budgeted income of E132,990,850. The report also gives the authoritative named list underpinning Eswatini's dual local-government structure: 'The 15 gazetted Urban Local Governments are as follows; Mbabane, Manzini, Nhlangano, Siteki, Pigg's Peak, Matsapha, Ezulwini, Mankayane, Hlathikhulu, Ngwenya, Vuvulane, Lavumisa, Malkerns, Buhleni and Hlane... urban areas are proclaimed under the Urban Government Act No.8 of 1969, which Act recognizes only three levels of local government, viz, Town Boards, Town Councils and Municipal Councils.' HOSTING/ACCESS CAVEAT: this document is hosted on parliament.gov.sz, a domain with a broken TLS certificate chain (fetch attempts failed with CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED / robots.txt fetch failures); it was retrieved this round only via a `curl --insecure` workaround. This is a technical-access issue with the hosting domain, not a content or authenticity problem -- the document itself is an authentic Ministry-authored report filed with Parliament.
reports.cadence_note: Annual ministry performance report to Parliament; this edition covers FY2024/25.

reports.title: Annual Report 2022/23 (including audited financial statements)
reports.description: Mbabane's own primary financial statements, not a third-party report. Income and Expenditure Statement for the year ended 31 March 2023: 'Revenue 134 088 900 [2023, E]... Other operating income 11 082 209... Grants and subvention 6 163 280... Total income 151 334 389,' with Note 3 stating 'Subvention received - Government of Eswatini 6 163 280... comprised of amounts received from the government of Eswatini during the year to finance operational costs.' Balance-sheet reserves (Note 13) show cumulative government funding including 'SLGP Grant 64 123 252' -- a named, quantified World Bank-financed Swaziland Local Government Project (SLGP) grant recorded in Mbabane's own books, alongside 'Government grants 96 726 377,' 'Government Foreign exchange Subvention 4 661 145' and 'Government grants - Urban Development Project (UDP) 85 611 499.' Narrative section on the performance-conditioned grant mechanism: 'Council's performance improved over previous year from 89% to 93% in accordance with the performance assessment by the Ministry for all urban local authorities in the country, adapted from the World Bank financed Swaziland Local Government Project (SLGP)... Municipalities obtaining a score of above 70% become eligible for Government funding for their capital projects.' Accounting policy note on government grants (Note 2.11): 'Grants from the government are recognized at their fair value when there is a reasonable assurance that the grant will be received... Government rates revenue received in respect of rates are offset against Government revenue debtors' -- corroborating (from a different fiscal year) the Ministry of Housing report's separate statement that Government owes Mbabane over E90 million in unpaid rates.
reports.cadence_note: Annual audited financial statements; this edition covers the FY ended 31 March 2023.

reports.title: Report of the Auditor General on the Consolidated Government Accounts of the Kingdom of Eswatini for the Financial Year Ended 31st March 2023
reports.publisher: Office of the Auditor-General, Kingdom of Eswatini (T. S. Matsebula, Auditor-General)
reports.description: Office of the Auditor-General's consolidated government accounts audit, naming Manzini Municipal Council with exact loan figures: 'The Financial Statements for Eswatini National Industrial Development Corporation (ENIDC) and Manzini Municipal Council for the year ended 31st March 2023 revealed that outstanding loans amounting to E33,551,816.00 were due to Government... The loan balance comprises of E25,564,222.00 for ENIDIC and E7,987,594.00 for the Manzini Municipal Council... Manzini Municipal Council / Government of Eswatini World Bank Loan / The Council received funding from the Government of Eswatini amounting E7,550,154.00. The terms and condition for this funding have not been finalised by the Council and the Government...' The same report also details regional-tier over-expenditure: 'There were unappropriated excess expenditures on Personnel Costs amounting to E16,065,231.65 incurred under the responsibility centres 1202- Manzini Regional Administrator (E7,048,536.72), 1204 - Lubombo Regional Administrator (E3,601,915.69), and 1203 - Shiselweni Regional Administrator (E5,414,779.24), in the financial year ended 31st March 2023' -- confirming region-level fiscal reporting with real appropriated-vs-actual figures (Hhohho notably absent from the over-expenditure finding). HOSTING CAVEAT: this exact copy is hosted on ifacweb.blob.core.windows.net (an IFAC-run accountability-index repository), not an oag.gov.sz/gov.sz domain; no official Eswatini-government-hosted copy could be located despite searching (the gov.sz Auditor-General page's report links are non-functional placeholders). The content is unambiguously an authentic Auditor-General-authored government document (named author, official 'KINGDOM OF ESWATINI' letterhead, standard OAG report format, dated 23 February 2024) -- a third-party-hosting issue, not a content or authenticity problem.
reports.cadence_note: Annual consolidated government accounts audit; this edition covers the FY ended 31 March 2023.

reports.title: Annual Report [Tinkhundla] 2025
reports.publisher: Ministry of Tinkhundla Administration and Development (MTAD), Kingdom of Eswatini
reports.description: Ministry of Tinkhundla Administration and Development's own FY2024/25 annual report to Parliament, with a per-region Regional Development Fund (RDF) budget table. On the Fund's origin: 'The Regional Development Fund (RDF) was established through Legal Notice Number 03 of 2015. The main objective of the fund is to alleviate and eventually eradicate poverty in each of the four regions of the Kingdom of Swaziland.' Table 2 ('RDF Projects Budget Performance Report,' 1 April-31 December 2024) gives, by region: 'HH 42,750,000.00 [Appropriated Budget 2024/25]... SHS 42,750,000.00... MNZ 51,300,000.00... LB 31,350,000.00' with a national total of 'E168,150,000.00' -- administered by the 'Microproject Programme Coordinating Unit (MPCU), a semi-autonomous unit under the Ministry of Economic Planning and Development.' On the separate Empowerment Fund (Tinkhundla operational upkeep): 'During the fiscal year 2024/2025, the Ministry received a total budget allocation of E7 095 000.00 for Empowerment Fund. In the second quarter the Ministry received a total of E3 322 500.00,' against a Statement of Receipts and Payments (period ended 30 November 2024) showing total payments of E5,094,314.59 -- a stated deficit of E1,655,224.03. HOSTING/ACCESS CAVEAT: like the companion Ministry of Housing report, this document is hosted on parliament.gov.sz, whose broken TLS certificate chain caused fetch failures (CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED / robots.txt errors); retrieved this round only via a `curl --insecure` workaround. Technical-access issue only, not a content problem.
reports.cadence_note: Annual ministry performance report to Parliament; this edition covers FY2024/25.

reports.title: Local Government: The Urban Government Act No. 8 of 1969
reports.description: Eswatini's (then Swaziland's) foundational urban-municipal-finance statute. Part IX ('Municipal Funds'), Section 86 ('Revenues of the council'): 'The revenues of a council shall consist of-- (a) all rates lawfully levied by the council; ... (g) all moneys paid to the council by the Government as contributions, grants, endowment or otherwise, except where such moneys are paid with a condition as to the purpose for which such moneys are paid...' -- establishing government grants as one permitted category of council revenue, though the Act itself states no allocation formula or percentage; the actual subvention/CIP-grant amounts are set by later Ministry of Housing administrative practice (see sz-mohud-annual-report-2024-25). Section 57(1) separately grants own-source fee authority: 'a council may charge fees for any service or facility provided by it or for any licence or permit issued by it.' HOSTING/QUALITY CAVEAT: this PDF is hosted by Gender Links (genderlinks.org.za), a South African NGO, not an Eswatini-government domain -- no official gov.sz/legislation portal copy could be located (the gov.sz 'ACTS' resources page does not list it). It is nonetheless authentic statutory text; its section numbering is independently corroborated by the Ministry of Housing's FY2024/25 report, which separately cites 'Section 115' and 'Section 8' of the same Act. The scanned/OCR'd PDF also has significant digit-garbling errors (e.g. '35.' for '85.', '36.' for '86.', page-footer range markers like 'ss.85-87' confirming the correct numbering despite garbled in-body digits); the quotes above are reproduced in cleaned form.
reports.cadence_note: One-off foundational statute (Act No. 8 of 1969), not a recurring publication.

reports.title: Implementation Completion and Results Report (IBRD-80030) on a Loan to the Government of Eswatini for the Swaziland Local Government Project (SLGP)
reports.description: World Bank Implementation Completion and Results Report (ICR00004807), closed December 2019. On Eswatini's dual local-government structure: 'The country has two categories of local government, namely Urban Local Governments (ULG) and Rural Local Governments, known as Tinkhundla... Formally, there are two City Councils (Manzini and Mbabane), five Town Councils and six Town Boards (five part of the Project)... The two City Councils are facing conditions of severe fiscal distress, characterized by weak revenue performance, high fixed operating costs, and ongoing deterioration in the quality of service delivery. Other Councils and Boards remain heavily reliant on central transfers to finance their expenditures... There is a total of 55 Tinkhundla or rural local governments.' On the project's limited lasting effect: 'There has been no action on the part of GOE to move towards a more stable fiscal transfer system and mainstreaming of performance-based grants (as recommended by reports produced by this project), and own source revenue in ULGs and Tinkundla remain very low.' A non-primary/context-flagged international-financial-institution report, but directly load-bearing here: Mbabane Municipal Council's own annual report explicitly states its capital-grant eligibility assessment is 'adapted from' this project (see the dependency edge below).
reports.cadence_note: One-off project completion report (ICR), published once at project closure (dated 20 December 2019).

reports.title: Harmonised Consumer Price Index: February 2019, Press Notice 02/2019
reports.description: Southern African Customs Union press notice publishing a regional Harmonised Consumer Price Index (HCPI). 'COMESA and SADC jointly developed a harmonised measure of consumer inflation, the Harmonised Consumer Price Index or HCPI,' with Table 2 ('SACU inflation rates (%) by COICOP categories') naming Eswatini's national figure individually: 'The highest annual rate was recorded in Eswatini (4.9%) followed by Namibia (4.6%).' Confirms SACU (of which Eswatini is a founding member) itself compiles a harmonised bulletin using COICOP categories with Eswatini's national CPI as a named per-country input line. NOTE: this is a February 2019 bulletin; a more current SACU HCPI edition was not located this round (see _dropped).
reports.cadence_note: SACU HCPI press notice numbered '02/2019', suggesting a possible regular (monthly?) publication cadence; not independently confirmed this round.

reports.title: Budget Speech 2025/26
reports.publisher: Ministry of Finance, Kingdom of Eswatini
reports.description: Eswatini's national Budget Speech for FY2025/26, presented by Minister of Finance Neal Rijkenberg on 14 February 2025. On the Regional/Rural Development Fund: 'In the 2025/26 financial year the Government will continue to allocate E177 million to the Rural Development Fund (RDF) with an additional E60 million towards clearing of the outstanding requests from the constituencies.' On the related community fund: 'E282.66 million has been allocated to the Micro Projects Community Development Fund (CDF).' NAMING CAVEAT: the Speech calls the fund the 'Rural Development Fund,' while the Ministry of Tinkhundla Administration's own FY2024/25 annual report (sz-mtad-annual-report-2024-25) and the fund's founding Legal Notice reference call it the 'Regional Development Fund' -- same RDF acronym, inconsistent full name across primary sources. The Speech gives only national aggregate figures, not a per-region or per-council breakdown.
reports.cadence_note: Annual national budget speech; this edition covers FY2025/26.

dependencies.basis: Mbabane's own annual report states its organizational performance assessment -- which directly gates capital-grant eligibility -- is 'adapted from the World Bank financed Swaziland Local Government Project (SLGP)': 'Council's performance improved over previous year from 89% to 93% in accordance with the performance assessment by the Ministry for all urban local authorities in the country, adapted from the World Bank financed Swaziland Local Government Project (SLGP)... Municipalities obtaining a score of above 70% become eligible for Government funding for their capital projects.'

The Ministry of Housing report attributes the legal basis of the 15 gazetted Urban Local Governments to the Act ('urban areas are proclaimed under the Urban Government Act No.8 of 1969, which Act recognizes only three levels of local government, viz, Town Boards, Town Councils and Municipal Councils') and separately cites specific sections by number: 'Section 115 of the Urban Government Act No.8 of 1969' (re: user-fee bye-laws) and 'Section 8 of the Urban Government Act No. 8 of 1969' (re: Councillor terms and conditions).

SACU's HCPI press notice compiles a per-country COICOP-based inflation table naming Eswatini's national annual inflation figure individually as an input: 'The highest annual rate was recorded in Eswatini (4.9%) followed by Namibia (4.6%),' drawn from the harmonised measure 'jointly developed' by COMESA and SADC from member states' own national CPIs, of which the Central Statistical Office's CPI is Eswatini's.

_dropped.edge: sz-mtad-annual-report-2024-25 RDF per-region split -> Legal Notice No. 03 of 2015 (RDF founding regulation)
_dropped.why: MTAD's own FY2024/25 report names 'Legal Notice Number 03 of 2015' as the RDF's founding instrument, and its Table 2 shows a per-region allocation (HH E42,750,000.00, SHS E42,750,000.00, MNZ E51,300,000.00, LB E31,350,000.00) that looks formula-shaped, but the underlying Legal Notice text could not be located on gov.sz, parliament.gov.sz, or via general web search this round, so it cannot be confirmed whether a stated split formula exists in the Notice itself versus the amounts being set by administrative discretion.

No official Eswatini-government-hosted copy of the Urban Government Act No. 8 of 1969 could be located this round (the gov.sz 'ACTS' resources page at https://www.gov.sz/index.php/resources/acts does not list it); the only working copy found is mirrored by Gender Links (genderlinks.org.za), a South African NGO. Recorded here as a hosting/provenance note rather than a dropped edge -- flagged in the node's own description as well.

The gov.sz Auditor-General homepage (https://www.gov.sz/index.php/home-auditor) exists but its report-category 'Read More' links have no functional URLs in the extracted HTML -- an effective dead end. The only working copy of the FY2023 consolidated accounts report found this round is hosted on ifacweb.blob.core.windows.net, an IFAC-run third-party repository. Flagged in the node's own description as well.

MOHUD's FY2024/25 report ties CIP capital-grant eligibility to councils' 'annual organizational performance assessment' but does not itself name the World Bank or the Swaziland Local Government Project as the methodology's origin -- only Mbabane's own annual report makes that explicit link. The methodology_depends_on edge in this file is therefore drawn only from Mbabane's report (sz-mbabane-annual-report-2022-23 -> sz-worldbank-slgp-icr-2019), not from MOHUD's, even though the same underlying mechanism plausibly governs both.

_dropped.why: Both documents describe the same fund (RDF acronym consistent across both) but the Budget Speech calls it the 'Rural Development Fund' while MTAD's own annual report and Legal Notice reference call it the 'Regional Development Fund' -- a naming inconsistency across primary sources, not treated as a dependency since the Speech gives only a forward-looking FY2025/26 national aggregate (E177m + E60m) rather than citing or recomputing MTAD's FY2024/25 per-region table (E168.15m total).

MOHUD's FY2024/25 report states Government owes Mbabane 'in excess of E90 million in rates' and that subventions to Mbabane and Manzini were 'immediately cut off' that reporting year. Mbabane's own FY2022/23 annual report (an earlier edition) independently corroborates the general government-rates-debtor and grant-conditionality mechanisms in its own accounting-policy notes but does not itself state the E90 million figure or the subvention cutoff (different fiscal years, and neither report cites the other by name) -- treated as corroborating context rather than a document-to-document dependency.
